messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: Synthetic canary 'canary-prober-eu-west-1' failure rate 62% over 5m -> paging on-call (rotation: praveen). Incident ID PD-7931 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Triggered: PD-7931 - Synthetic probes failing in eu-west-1 - severity: P2
praveen (oncall): acked the alert :white_check_mark: - I'm on it, joining the thread.
praveen (oncall): quick context: this is the prober job we run from k8s CronJob 'canary-prober' that hits /health and token-refresh endpoints. Getting a lot of 401s.
maya (eng-runtime): noted, I saw an uptick in probe 401s starting ~10:03 UTC. Could be the token rotation job that ran at 09:58.
sam (eng-sre): adding logs from the prober pod (last 5 lines):
```
2026-03-14T10:04:11Z prober INFO probe_request id=abc123 status=401 body="unauthorized: token invalid"
2026-03-14T10:04:12Z prober INFO token_refresh error=401 response="{"error":"invalid_client"}"
2026-03-14T10:04:13Z prober INFO probe_request id=abc124 status=401
2026-03-14T10:04:15Z prober WARN backoff sleeping=5s
2026-03-14T10:04:20Z prober INFO probe_request id=abc125 status=200
```
praveen (oncall): interesting, occasional 200s. Looks like token refresh failing for many workers but not all. Could be ratelimit or a bad token pair.
jess (product): any customer-facing impact? We got an inbound question from support about a canary dashboard flapping. Nobody reported user errors.
maya (eng-runtime): initial assessment: this affects synthetic checks only. Hosted API traffic is fine; runtime logs show normal auth success for serving requests. This looks isolated to the prober's token refresh path (service account + short-lived token exchange).
praveen (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) suppress noisy pager for the canary to stop paging rotation (but keep SLO metrics). 2) trigger prober to use fallback cached token to reduce failures. 3) escalate to runtime team for root cause.
sre-rotation-bot: auto-handoff scheduled -> next oncall: maya in 28m.
praveen (oncall): executing suppression:
```
# silence in OpsMode for 30m
curl -X POST "https://ops-console/api/alerts/silence" -d '{"alert":"canary-failure","duration":1800}'
```
praveen (oncall): suppression applied :no_bell: - will still log all failures, just not page.
maya (eng-runtime): temporary fix: patching prober deployment to reuse previous token path. Applying a 1-line change to environment to point PROBER_TOKEN_PATH -> /mnt/fallback/token. Doing a rollout restart of canary prober.
sam (eng-sre): command run: `kubectl -n infra set env job/canary-prober PROBER_TOKEN_PATH=/mnt/fallback/token` -> then `kubectl -n infra rollout restart job/canary-prober`

(rolling restart trace)
```
job "canary-prober" restarted: 3 pods terminating, 3 pods starting
pod/canary-prober-9j2lz logs: token loaded from /mnt/fallback/token, probe OK
```
praveen (oncall): new prober pods show success. Failure rate dropped to ~3% over 5m. Good sign.
maya (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: automated token rotation job published new client_secret to KMS but the prober's sidecar that mirrors secrets lagged behind due to a kubelet restart window; prober moved to exchange endpoint while missing updated client creds -> 401. We'll do the full postmortem but immediate fix is in place.
jess (product): TL;DR for support: "Synthetic canaries in eu-west-1 experienced token-refresh failures after an automated secret rotation. No customer-facing API errors were observed. We suppressed pages to avoid oncall churn and patched the prober to use fallback tokens while we investigate."
praveen (oncall): escalation: opening PD-7931 with details and assigning to eng-runtime (maya).
praveen (oncall): creating follow-ups:
- eng-runtime: verify secret sync logic and add guard against exchange attempts when client_secret missing
- infra: add probe health metric that differentiates auth failures vs endpoint errors
- SRE: add a 5m aggregation rule to avoid immediate paging for transient spike of synthetic failures

maya (eng-runtime): accepted PD-7931, will dig into secret-mirror controller logs and KMS audit trail. ETA 3h for deeper root cause.
sam (eng-sre): re-enabled paging (but with higher threshold) to catch real infra issues: set paging threshold from 5m/20% -> 10m/25% for the canary to reduce noise.
praveen (oncall): closing the active page loop, marking incident as "mitigated (noise)". Will update PD when root cause identified. Thanks all for quick coord :raised_hands:

-- follow-up notes (to be captured in incident doc) --
1) Timeline: 09:58 secret rotation -> 10:03 probe 401 spike -> 10:06 PD pages -> 10:07 suppression -> 10:10 prober rollback to fallback token -> 10:14 failures drop to baseline -> 10:25 paging thresholds adjusted
2) Impact: Synthetic canaries in eu-west-1 only; no customer-facing errors, no tenant API requests failed. False-positive alerting created oncall churn.
3) Action items: (a) eng-runtime: add preflight check in prober to assert token refresh success before sending mixture of live probes (b) infra: improve secret mirror reliability and add alert on secret-staleness (c) product/sre: tune synthetic alerting to require sustained failure across shards before paging.

praveen (oncall): I'll hand this over to maya (eng-runtime) for root cause. Handoff ETA 28m. If anything changes ping this thread or PD.
maya (eng-runtime): acknowledged, taking ownership. I'll post updates here and in PD-7931.

incident-bot: Incident PD-7931 status -> mitigated (no customer impact). Archived noise page.
